text:
Alisha R.: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) opened a support ticket — Dedicated pool reporting sharp throughput drop starting ~08:10 UTC. They see lots of 429s and tail latency spikes. I forwarded logs.

Devin H.: tagging infra — which dedicated pool? any recent deploys or autoscale events? @Jun Park

Jun Park: pool redwood-dedicated-eu-4. No deploys in last 24h. Autoscaler shows multiple small scaleups but pods never reached expected batch sizes. SRE Bot reports GPU util dip.

SRE Bot: Alert: continuous_batcher.backlog > 1000 for 16m on redwood-dedicated-eu-4. avg_batch_tokens dropped from 640 -> 48 over last 30m. (link to metrics)

Maria K.: Interesting — avg_batch_tokens = 48 is way below max_batch_tokens. Could be scheduler preemption or noisy neighbor causing LKVM scheduling. Any tail latencies on enqueue? can we get request traces?

Support Bot: Customer provided repro: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"gptx-dedicated-v1","prompt":"x","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}' -> returns 429 or 200 with 12s first token.

Alisha R.: They said this affects ~20% of requests intermittently, mostly at 90-150 RPS. Billing not broken, but SLA complaints.

Devin H.: I pulled scheduler logs. Saw lots of single-request batches created by continuous-batcher because queue window closed early. A noisy tenant had extremely short-loop calls causing rapid enqueue/dequeue churn. This prevented larger batches from forming.

Jun Park: Possible mitigations: raise continuous_batcher.window_ms from 6 -> 12 for this pool, and increase max_batch_tokens soft-limit. Also consider per-tenant smoothing: request coalescing for hot clients.

Maria K.: Quick repro plan: 1) Toggle window_ms to 12 temporarily, 2) set max_batch_tokens to 1024, 3) watch avg_batch_tokens and tail latency. If improves, rollout config change and schedule tenant rate-limits.

Alisha R.: Can someone run the toggle? customer is ok with a maintenance window in 15m.

Devin H.: I'll apply the temporary change to redwood-dedicated-eu-4 now and watch. Command I run:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap continuous-batcher-config -p '{"data":{"window_ms":"12","max_batch_tokens":"1024"}}'
```

SRE Bot: Patch applied to configmap at 1799991750. Autoscaler state stable. Beginning 10m observation.

Jun Park: Also enabling per-GPU noisy-tenant metrics: label hot-tenants and sample queueing latency by tenant id.

SRE Bot: Metrics update: avg_batch_tokens -> 512 after 6m, continuous_batcher.backlog -> 120, 429 rate down 70%.

Alisha R.: Customer reports major improvement. Still seeing occasional spikes but much better. They asked for permanent fix and whether we should throttle the noisy client.

Maria K.: Next steps: 1) rollback not needed, make window_ms=12 permanent for pool; 2) add tenant-level enforcement for pathological patterns (burst limiter), 3) follow-up postmortem + runbook for similar escalations.

Devin H.: I'll create PR with config change + add tenant-rate-limit quick-fix circuit. Assigning to Jun for follow-up instrumentation. :thumbsup:

Jun Park: Got it. I'll also add an alert when avg_batch_tokens < 200 for >5m so we catch this earlier.

Alisha R.: Thanks all. Closing support escalation once PR merges and customer confirms in 24h. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
